purchasing-digitalization.context: A construction company with several divisions involved in purchasing goods.
purchasing-digitalization.problem: Purchase requests ran on Excel and paper. Data was scattered or duplicated, approvals were slow, divisions weren't in sync, and the status from request to payment was hard to track or audit.
purchasing-digitalization.solution: One AppSheet app unifying the whole flow: automatic request numbering, relational tables, role-based access (requester, approver, purchasing, finance), and a real-time status dashboard, with data stored in Google Sheets and accessible on phone or desktop.

ai-messaging-ticketing.context: A messaging assistant serving customers on WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook, with escalation tickets routed to a team.
ai-messaging-ticketing.problem: Messages arrive from several channels in free form, while the team only needs structured data from each customer. The team also needs to see which tickets pile up and who owns them, and the bot needs guard rails so it does not answer spam or loop with other automated services.
ai-messaging-ticketing.solution: A per-customer state machine stored in the database: entry gate, numbered menu, data collection, then a ticket whose recipients come from database configuration. AI is used in a limited way (fallback intent classification, spam screening, a daily report). A web app shows chats, tickets, and workflow controls with per-owner access.

brand-intelligence.context: A brand-monitoring service for clients who want to know how customers talk about their brand and how it compares with competitors.
brand-intelligence.problem: Brand conversations were scattered across platforms and read by hand. A sudden complaint or a rising competitor took too long to spot, and every client needed their own view of the data.
brand-intelligence.solution: A web dashboard that collects posts and comments from social platforms for each brand, scores sentiment, compares competitors by share of voice, flags crisis and opportunity anomalies, and compiles daily digests and period reports. Keyword proposals go through an approval step, and three user roles see only their own brands.

ai-video-agent.context: A production system for short, user-generated-content-style product videos for a team: staff prepare characters and products in a web app, and videos are produced by an agent on a production laptop or by a video model through an API.
ai-video-agent.problem: The first prototype called automation workflows straight from the browser, step by step, with no queue, no central approval, and no cost tracking. Producing videos at volume with a consistent character, safe product claims, and controlled spend was not possible that way.
ai-video-agent.solution: Work is stored as a queue in the database. Staff build a panel plan, storyboard, and video JSON, then approve; the database refuses to queue a batch when the submit requirements are incomplete. Built-in safeguards: admin approval for risky products, daily and per-batch limits, and a claim-word checker on the script. The agent claims tasks with row locking, stops and reports when a human is needed, and retries with backoff. Later stages (clip merging, voice, on-screen text, ambient sound, upscaling) run as their own task queues, and the cost of each process is recorded.
ai-video-agent.learning: Safeguards that live only in the interface can be bypassed: testing showed staff could insert a job straight into the queue and forge the admin approval. So admin approval for risky products (children and health claims) and the daily and per-batch limits are enforced in the database, while the claim-word checker is still only an interface guard. Third-party services have limits (activity flags, quotas, model version retirements), so the agent stops and reports when a human is needed, with random pacing and bounded retries.
